description: Contests whose figures fail a rule of scripts/check/rules/contest-arithmetic.mjs because the source itself does not add up (or follows a rule of its own), checked against the source named. Each entry: sourceFile (or "*" with electionKey for a whole election), rule, reason, source. Transcription errors are not listed here: they are fixed in source-checked-fixes.json.

entries.reason: The 1918 election was a block vote: Cork City returned two members and each voter had two votes, so the 60,722 votes cast exceed the 45,017 electors; the turnout is of voters, not votes.
entries.source: ElectionsIreland.org, 1918 Cork City; Walker, Parliamentary Election Results in Ireland 1801-1922

entries.reason: The 52 are the corporation's voters (History of Parliament, 1831); the 70 tendered freemen's votes counted here were not on that roll.
entries.source: History of Parliament 1820-1832, Coleraine

entries.reason: Brydges was returned on the corporation's 16 votes; Copeland's 70 were freemen's votes tendered and rejected at the poll. On petition Brydges was unseated and Copeland declared elected (4 August 1831). The contest's note says so.
entries.source: Walker, Parliamentary Election Results in Ireland 1801-1922; History of Parliament 1820-1832, Coleraine

entries.reason: Walker prints 2,507 votes (1,210 + 759 + 538) against 2,438 registered electors, a turnout of 102.8%; Wikipedia notes the discrepancy. Kept as printed.
entries.source: Walker, Parliamentary Election Results in Ireland 1801-1922; Wikipedia, Dublin University (constituency)

entries.reason: ElectionsIreland.org gives Leinster 4 seats and a quota of 61,380 (306,896 / 5 + 1), and Wikipedia repeats the quota; Leinster returned 3 MEPs in 1979 (both sources list 3 elected), for which the quota would be 76,725. The source's quota is kept.
entries.source: ElectionsIreland.org, result.cfm?election=1979E&cons=526; Wikipedia, 1979 European Parliament election in Ireland

entries.reason: The Donegal Democrat's first preferences add up to 13,208 against its printed valid poll of 13,030; its quota of 1,890 fits 13,208. Figures kept as printed (the record says so).
entries.source: Donegal Democrat, 15 June 1979, p. 14 (Irish Newspaper Archives)

entries.reason: The printed quota 1,890 is floor(13,208 / 7) + 1, from the printed first preferences, not the printed valid poll of 13,030.
entries.source: Donegal Democrat, 15 June 1979, p. 14 (Irish Newspaper Archives)

entries.reason: The Leinster Leader prints a total poll of 12,671, 232 spoilt and a valid poll of 12,436 (12,668).
entries.source: Leinster Leader, 16 June 1979, p. 7 (Irish Newspaper Archives)

entries.reason: The Leinster Leader's first preferences add up to 12,439 against its printed valid poll of 12,436.
entries.source: Leinster Leader, 16 June 1979, p. 7 (Irish Newspaper Archives)

entries.reason: The Leinster Leader's first preferences add up to 7,347 against its printed valid poll of 7,387.

entries.reason: After the recount the printed first preferences add up to 4,324 against the stated valid poll of 4,325 (the record's source note).
entries.source: Roscommon Herald, 28 June 1985, p. 9 (Irish Newspaper Archives)

entries.reason: The printed first preferences add up to 12,448 against the stated valid poll of 12,447 (the record's source note).

entries.reason: The Roscommon Herald's first preferences add up to 4,073, one short of its valid poll of 4,074; the Irish Independent's McGreal 580 would balance but the Herald's 579 agrees with its own second count (the record's source note).
entries.source: Roscommon Herald, 28 June 1985, p. 9; Irish Independent, 22 June 1985, p. 8 (Irish Newspaper Archives)

entries.reason: The Chief Electoral Officer's sheet prints Fraser Agnew's seventh-stage total as 3,529.21 (3,370.55 + 158.46 = 3,529.01) and his ninth as 4,946.21 (3,847.08 + 1,117.13 = 4,964.21; the tenth, 4,965.31, follows from 4,964.21). Kept as printed.
entries.source: Election to the New Northern Ireland Assembly 1998, Belfast North continuation sheet (booklet p. 8)

entries.reason: The sheet prints Pat McNamee's seventh-stage total as 5,534.53 where 5,332.53 + 12 = 5,344.53. Kept as printed, with a source note.
entries.source: Election to the New Northern Ireland Assembly 1998, Newry and Armagh continuation sheet (booklet p. 29)

entries.reason: The sheet prints Aidan Larkin's fifth-stage total as 3,987.75 where 3,967.51 + 20.44 = 3,987.95. Kept as printed, with a source note.
entries.source: Convention Elections 1975, Mid-Ulster result sheet (booklet p. 25)

entries.reason: The sheet gives Anthony Williamson a fifth-stage transfer of 206 and a total of 1,882.80 (1,676.08 + 206 = 1,882.08). Kept as printed, with a source note.
entries.source: Convention Elections 1975, South Down result sheet (booklet p. 19)

entries.reason: The Electoral Office's result sheet prints 2,615 votes polled with 2,578 valid and 31 invalid (2,609); its 27.67% poll is 2,615 of the 9,449 electors, so the slip is in the valid or invalid figure, and the first preferences add up to 2,578. The figures are kept as printed.
entries.source: Electoral Office for Northern Ireland, Antrim Town by-election result sheet, 30 June 1987 (eoni.org.uk, Internet Archive capture of 6 August 2019)

entries.reason: The Electoral Office's booklet prints a quota one above the Droop quota (3,052 valid votes, 5 seats: floor(3,052 / 6) + 1 = 509); its other header figures are as Civgraph shows them, and the count was run on the printed quota.
entries.source: Local Government Election Results 1993, Carrickfergus: Carrick Castle (PDF p. 110), https://web.archive.org/web/20210709183748id_/https://www.eoni.org.uk/getmedia/b0d9bd01-b804-48bd-8641-9d763ec66466/local_government_election_results_1993
